note: Matriculation-friendly physical and chemical properties. Boiling points are standard atmospheric values (°C). Solubility and state refer to room temperature (~25 °C) unless noted.

compounds.name: Methane
compounds.combustion: Burns with a clean blue flame to give CO2 and H2O
compounds.note: Main component of natural gas.

compounds.name: Ethane
compounds.solubility: Insoluble in water; soluble in organic solvents
compounds.combustion: Clean combustion to CO2 and H2O
compounds.note: Saturated hydrocarbon; only substitution reactions under UV with halogens.

compounds.name: Propane
compounds.combustion: Clean combustion; used as bottled fuel (LPG with butane)
compounds.note: Boiling point rises as carbon chain length increases.

compounds.name: Butane
compounds.combustion: Clean combustion to CO2 and H2O
compounds.note: Easily liquefied under pressure for portable fuels.

compounds.name: Pentane
compounds.note: First straight-chain alkane that is liquid at room temperature.

compounds.name: Ethene
compounds.combustion: Burns with a luminous/sooty flame more readily than ethane
compounds.note: Unsaturated; undergoes addition reactions (Br2 decolourises).

compounds.name: Propene
compounds.combustion: Luminous flame; addition reactions typical of alkenes
compounds.note: Important feedstock for polypropylene.

compounds.name: Ethyne
compounds.solubility: Slightly soluble in water; more soluble in acetone
compounds.combustion: Very sooty luminous flame; oxy-acetylene welding uses ethyne
compounds.note: Triple bond; acidic terminal hydrogen can be replaced by metals.

compounds.name: Propyne
compounds.combustion: Sooty flame; addition across the triple bond
compounds.note: Also called methylacetylene.

compounds.name: Methanol
compounds.combustion: Burns with a clean blue flame; toxic vapour
compounds.note: Much higher boiling point than methane because of hydrogen bonding.

compounds.name: Ethanol
compounds.combustion: Clean blue flame; used as a biofuel and solvent
compounds.note: Boiling point higher than ethane for the same reason — intermolecular H-bonds.

compounds.name: Propan-1-ol
compounds.note: Primary alcohol; oxidised to propanal then propanoic acid.

compounds.name: Propan-2-ol
compounds.note: Secondary alcohol; oxidised to propanone (not further).

compounds.name: Methanal
compounds.note: Simplest aldehyde; used to preserve biological specimens.

compounds.name: Ethanal
compounds.note: Easily oxidised to ethanoic acid.

compounds.name: Propanone
compounds.note: Ketones resist mild oxidation compared with aldehydes.

compounds.name: Methanoic acid
compounds.note: Present in ant and bee stings; stronger than ethanoic acid.

compounds.name: Ethanoic acid
compounds.combustion: Burns; vinegar is dilute aqueous ethanoic acid (~4–8%)
compounds.note: High BP due to dimer hydrogen bonding between acid molecules.

compounds.name: Propanoic acid
compounds.note: Boiling points of carboxylic acids rise with chain length.

compounds.name: Methyl ethanoate
compounds.note: Esters have lower boiling points than the parent acids (no H-bonding between molecules).

compounds.name: Ethyl ethanoate
compounds.note: Common organic solvent; made by esterification of ethanoic acid with ethanol.

compounds.name: Methoxymethane
compounds.note: Isomer of ethanol but much lower boiling point (no OH hydrogen bonding).

compounds.name: Methoxyethane
compounds.note: Functional isomer of propanols.

compounds.name: Chloromethane
compounds.combustion: Flammable; halogenated products on incomplete combustion
compounds.note: Substitution product of methane with chlorine (UV).

compounds.name: Chloroethane
compounds.note: Useful intermediate; denser than related hydrocarbons when liquefied.

compounds.name: Bromoethane
compounds.note: Denser than water; classic nucleophilic substitution substrate in advanced work.
